items.note: Petition committee report P492 (dated 27 Oct 2025, published 31 Oct 2025), section 2.3 (statement of the BVD representative): permit went from CHF 140 to 284 at the start of 2019 and demand fell; the one-permit-per-person limit in force since 2019 also contributed to the reduction. Title matches the page.

Press release dated 22.10.2019: from 1 Nov 2019 the evening rate in City, Steinen and Elisabethen starts two hours earlier, CHF 2/h from 17:00 to 24:00; daytime stays CHF 3/h; 'vorerst auf zwei Jahre befristet'. The text says it was introduced for two years and does not say it still applies. Title matches.

Press release dated 11.01.2021 supports cashless per-minute payment, buying blue-zone visitor permits and the reminder function. But it does not say permits could be bought 'in person'; it says coins at the meter, and visitor permits online or at BVB ticket machines, remain available. The app was developed by the Kantonspolizei with the Amt fuer Mobilitaet and Tiefbauamt.
items.corrected_text: In January 2021 the canton's police launched the ParkSmart Basel app for cashless, per-minute payment at parking meters and for buying blue-zone visitor permits, with a reminder before parking time runs out. Paying with coins at the meter and buying visitor permits online or at BVB ticket machines remained possible.

items.note: Direct curl was blocked by Cloudflare; read through WebFetch. The 15.04.2021 update says parliament approved CHF 11.4m as a conditionally repayable interest-free loan for the 200 stations IWB is to install and operate (170 AC, 30 DC by 2026), and referred to the government a motion asking for 2,000 charge points in publicly accessible garages in addition. The article does not say the stations are 'mainly on public land' or call them 'public'; it calls them neighbourhood charging stations (Quartier-Ladestationen). Title matches (article dated 24.03.2021, update 15.04.2021).
items.corrected_text: In April 2021 the cantonal parliament approved CHF 11.4 million as a conditionally repayable, interest-free loan so that IWB could install and operate 200 neighbourhood charging stations (170 AC and 30 DC) by 2026. According to the report, parliament also referred to the government a motion asking for a further 2,000 charge points in publicly accessible garages.

items.note: SRF article (timestamp 25.09.2021, radio segment 26.09.2021; the vote day was 26 Sept 2021, so 2021-09 is right). Initiative 'fuer erschwingliche Parkgebuehren' by ACS/TCS sought to reverse the 2019 increase in parking fees on public land; rejected with 55.7% no (results box) / 55.8% (body text), so 'about 56%' holds. Title matches.

Implenia news item dated 05.01.2022: opened mid-December at St. Alban-Graben 3a, 350 spaces on four levels, open 24/7, e-charging stations; built by Implenia as general contractor for a Credit Suisse Asset Management real estate fund. Title matches.

Grosser Rat press release dated 13.06.2022: 2013 decision (13 Mar 2013) required removal of at least 210 spaces on public land within about 500 m; only 104 counted by end of May 2022; UVEK and BVD agreed on 70 more by end 2022 and a flexible solution for the remaining 36. Opening on 17 Dec 2021 is also stated. Title matches.

Government press release dated 18.06.2024: from 1 Jan 2025 resident permits CHF 332 (<3.90 m), 422 (medium, from 284), 512 (>4.90 m); commuter permits 860/950/1,040; second step on 1 Jan 2027 to 380/560/740. Text is framed as an announcement, not as the current price, so known issue (a) does not arise. Title matches.

Same 18.06.2024 release. It says meter fees will 'in future' be set per meter by location, surrounding uses and occupancy, at four levels from CHF 1 to 4/h, replacing the fee zones, and that the maximum possible rate rises from CHF 3 to 4. But it only says the government PLANS to apply the CHF 4 rate at a few busy central spots such as the Birsigparkplatz or Claragraben; it does not say the rise took place there. It also gives no separate effective date for the meter change (only that the first tariff increase is on 1 Jan 2025). The date has been changed to the announcement.
items.corrected_text: The June 2024 announcement said parking-meter fees would in future be set for each meter by location, nearby uses and occupancy, at four levels from CHF 1 to 4 per hour, replacing the fixed fee zones. The maximum possible rate would rise from CHF 3 to 4 per hour, which the government planned to use only at a few busy central spots such as the Birsigparkplatz or Claragraben.

items.note: Direct curl was blocked (Access Denied); read through WebFetch. Federal press release dated 16 Oct 2024: the Wertfreigrenze in travel falls from CHF 300 to 150 per person per day from 1 Jan 2025, to meet two cantonal initiatives aimed at reducing shopping tourism. Title matches. The 2025-01 date is the effective date.

Government report on the Anzug (decision of 3 Feb 2026, published 6 Feb 2026): the Einwohnergemeinde der Stadt Basel bought the Horburg garage from Novartis in December 2024 (early reversion of the building right); after safety and upgrade works, one of three sections is planned to open to long-term renters from Q2 2026. The Anzug notes use had been restricted to employees. The page does not name 'Kleinbasel'; it places the garage by the Horburgpark in the Klybeck area. Title matches.
items.corrected_text: In December 2024 the municipality of Basel bought the Horburg garage by the Horburgpark from Novartis, whose use of it had been limited to employees. After safety and upgrade works, one of its three sections was planned to open to long-term renters from the second quarter of 2026.

items.note: BVD press release dated 02.07.2025. Supported: 498 street spaces lost Nov 2022 to Nov 2024 per the register, de facto about 350 after two recording effects; about 2,000 private spaces in 35 new buildings completed in 2023-2024; first pilot expected from September 2025. Not supported: the pilot is about 50 underground spaces at PSP Swiss Property, Hochstrasse 16, for shared use (Mehrfachnutzung), bookable via Share-P only. The page does not say 'office garage' or 'residents' for this pilot, and Parcandi is named separately as an app offering other private spaces, not as part of the pilot. Title matches.
items.corrected_text: The transport department reported that, after correcting for two recording changes, street parking fell by about 350 spaces between November 2022 and November 2024, while about 2,000 private spaces were built in 35 new buildings completed in 2023 and 2024. A first pilot for shared use of private parking, about 50 underground spaces at Hochstrasse 16 rentable through the Share-P platform, was expected to start in September 2025.

items.note: Government press release dated 14.10.2025: concept for Quartierparkings; most urgent need in Kleinbasel, met by partly converting the existing Novartis Klybeck garage and a new one in the planned Messehalle 3 development; further need in eastern Gundeldingen (Dreispitz area) and eastern Iselin (Colmarerstrasse/Wasgenring), with no concrete projects yet; Mobility Fund ordinance amended to allow contributions of up to 40% of construction costs; tariffs to follow market prices of private parking. Title matches.

Same P492 report (27 Oct 2025): BVD representative said street spaces fell by about 2,000 to 26,000 between 2015 and 2024; about 80,000 spaces on private land including public garages; Amt fuer Mobilitaet expects about 2,000 fewer resident permits at end 2025 than end 2024; petitioners cited the Price Supervisor's CHF 322 maximum. Title matches.

Art Basel story (German version): 2025 edition with 289 galleries from 42 countries and territories, 88,000 visitors over preview and public days; June dates (19-20 June) and the Messeplatz/Halle 1.0 venue appear on the page. Page title is 'Art Basel's 2025 edition concludes on a high note'; matches.
Suedostschweiz, 'Agentur sda', 22.06.2026: 90,000 visitors, 290 galleries from 43 countries, audience from 103 countries. Title matches.

Cantonal page (content updated 20.07.2026): about 4,300 spaces; lists City, Elisabethen, Steinen, St. Jakob, Storchen, ELYS, U70, Horburg; 22 kW Swisscharge stations in cooperation with IWB in five garages: Steinen 6, Elisabethen 7 (2+5), City 8, Storchen 1, St. Jakob 2. Title matches.

corrected_summary: In Basel-Stadt the annual resident parking permit rose from CHF 140 to CHF 284 at the start of 2019, and in September 2021 voters rejected an initiative to reverse the 2019 increase in parking fees. Since 1 January 2025 resident permit fees depend on vehicle length, with a second increase announced for 2027, and in October 2025 the government presented a concept for neighbourhood garages to move street parking onto private land; the municipality bought the Horburg garage from Novartis in December 2024. Parking Kunstmuseum opened in December 2021 with 350 spaces, linked to a requirement to remove 210 nearby street spaces.
